_meta.rule: Nothing here changes a pipeline output. Saffire: the lowest and the highest stored reading of column 'Ambient Pressure' of each linked workbook (data/pipeline/raw_values.csv) are converted with the factor below and placed in the pressure bins of spec/coverage.json and the pressure ranges of spec/scenarios.json. SAME-R: the stored values of raw_values.csv that are tied to a test are counted per size statistic; a stored 0 and an error string are not counted as a value.
_meta.not_adopted: Not adopted: a decision of the team's human lead.

saffire_pressure.factor_source: spec/findings.json _meta.units.psi_to_kpa (1 psi = 6.894757 kPa); the rules for the experimental tables (spec/sources.json) hold no psia factor
saffire_pressure.arithmetic: The conversion of the lowest and the highest reading (reading x factor, rounded to 4 decimals) is the only arithmetic. No mean, no value at ignition and no interpolation is computed.
saffire_pressure.what_min_kpa_and_max_kpa_are: min_kpa and max_kpa are a unit conversion of the lowest and the highest stored reading of a whole logging window of one workbook (one per sample); they are not a test pressure, not the pressure at ignition, and no column states when the flame ignited.

saffire_pressure.sentence_choice: Which reading would stand for a test (the first, the lowest, the one at ignition) is a choice that no file makes; no column of the workbooks states when the flame ignited. The sensor workbooks have igniter channels (for example 'Igniter Current', 'Igniter Voltage', 'Igniter Power Enable'), which were not read.

same_r_particle_size.statistic_names: The keys of same_statistic_classes are the team's short names for groups of stored headers. The cells say only 'M1/M0 (micro-m)--AMD' or '--CMD'; where both labels exist for one test inside the results workbook the stored values are equal, which is why they are one group; what AMD and CMD stand for is not written in the workbook. 'Hatch Choate Dg' has no unit in any header; sheet 'ICES 2012 Paper data table' holds 0.09 in M5 (Hatch Choate Dg) next to 90 in Q5 ('Geom.Mean Diam. (nm)'), and the workbook does not state the unit. A key is a stored header name, not the quantity smoke_particle_size_um.
same_r_particle_size.files_differ: For every test with stored values in both the results workbook and the TEM workbook the values of the same statistic differ: the TEM cells are cached values of external references to a version of the results workbook that is not in PSI ([2]SAME R Results), and its 'Hatch Choate Dg' column O refers to column BM, which in the PSI results workbook is headed 'Hatch Choate Sigma g' (BM2), not 'Hatch Choate Dg' (BN2). A test counts as having a value if one positive value is stored in either file, whether or not the files agree.
same_r_particle_size.would_the_count_change: The count of D2 does not change: no value is adopted, so tests.csv holds no smoke_particle_size_um and D2 keeps no counted test. If one statistic were adopted as smoke_particle_size_um, a D2 test would be counted only where it also meets every required condition (fuel_material, flow_cms, aging_time_s) under a supported link; 'statistics' gives that number per statistic. Headers without a unit (AMD, CMD, Hatch Choate Dg) would also need a unit stated by a document, and the investigators name more than one statistic, so choosing one is part of the decision.

flex_test_sheets.state: read from NASA's file, not adopted
flex_test_sheets.not_adopted: Not adopted: a decision of the team's human lead.
flex_test_sheets.written_from: data/pipeline/raw_values.csv (extraction flex_test_sheet), compared with data/psi/experimental_tables/PSI-69_Experimental table_FLEX.csv as the file writes it; per field: data/pipeline/flex_sheet_vs_table.csv
flex_test_sheets.tie_rule: the CIR test number printed inside the sheet equals the table's 'FLEX Identifier' (first label), and a second field agrees: the FLEX number of the sheet's first line equals 'FLEX Test #', or, where it does not, the test date of the sheet equals the table's 'Test Date'. tie_state:   identifier_and_number   identifier and FLEX number name the same row   identifier_and_date     identifier and date name one row; the FLEX number                           names another row or none (the two numberings differ)   identifier_only         the identifier names rows, no second field agrees   identifier_not_in_table the identifier is in no row A sheet is tied (test_id filled) only for the first two states. Nothing read here becomes a value of tests.csv or enters a count.
flex_test_sheets.comparison_rule: text: equal as written; date and time: the same day or clock time; numbers: equal, or within half a unit of the last decimal the sheet writes (pressure: sheet atm against table mmHg / 760); a nan, blank, dash or text on either side is compared by form only

cases.sheet_value_as_written: out of all FOVs, no means to even estimate

numbering_crosswalk.rule: sheets whose number in the file name is not the 'FLEX Test #' of the table row the sheet is tied to (or that are not tied)

flex_test_sheets.what_the_codes_mean: No file opened says what nan, 0.00, a blank or a dash mean, or whether the sheet's line 'Dext (mm)' is the visible-flame extinction diameter of the table.
